200: Bizenghast by M. Alice LeGrow (Tokyopop) is a gothic horror story with a fairy-tale feel. After losing her parents, Dinah goes to live with her aunt in Bizenghast, a crumbling town full of restless spirits. When she and her friend Vincent explore an old mausoleum, Dinah ends up bound by a contract that forces her to return every night to free the ghosts trapped inside. It suits readers who like spooky riddles and dark, ornate art.
204: Manga Classics: Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare, adapted by Crystal S. Chan with art by Julien Choy (Manga Classics), is a faithful retelling of the classic tragedy. In Verona, the feuding Montague and Capulet families keep the streets on edge. When young Romeo slips into a Capulet party, he meets Juliet, and the two fall in love at first sight. It is a friendly way into Shakespeare for students and a fresh take for longtime fans.
211: Gosick by Kazuki Sakuraba (Tokyopop) is a mystery light novel set in a small European kingdom in the 1920s. Kazuya Kujo, a serious Japanese exchange student at St. Marguerite Academy, keeps climbing to the top of the library tower, where he finds Victorique, a tiny, sharp-tongued girl with a brilliant mind. When real crimes come their way, she solves them while he does the legwork. Readers who enjoy classic whodunits and odd-couple pairings will feel at home.
212: Brigadoon by Nozomi Watase (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi drama set in 1960s Japan. Marin Asagi is a cheerful orphan girl living in a quiet neighborhood when a strange other world called Brigadoon suddenly appears in the sky. Dangerous creatures start hunting her, and a mysterious blue warrior named Melan Blue arrives to protect her. It mixes a coming-of-age story with monster battles, and fans of the anime will recognize its warm, bittersweet mood.
213: Rohan at the Louvre by Hirohiko Araki (NBM) is a supernatural mystery starring Rohan Kishibe, the eccentric manga artist from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure. Years ago, a young woman told teenage Rohan about the blackest painting in the world, a cursed work hidden somewhere in the Louvre. Now a successful artist, he travels to Paris to find it. This standalone story is a great pick for JoJo fans and for anyone who loves art, museums, and eerie mysteries.
214: Basilisk by Masaki Segawa (Del Rey) is a dark historical action series about rival ninja clans. In 1614, the Iga and Koga clans have been held to a truce for years, and the young heirs Gennosuke and Oboro are in love and hope to unite their families. Then the shogunate lifts the truce and orders ten fighters from each side to battle to the death. It is a gripping read for fans of ninja stories and tragic romance.
215: Gyo by Junji Ito (Viz Media) is a horror story about the ocean coming ashore. While vacationing in Okinawa, Tadashi and his girlfriend Kaori notice a terrible smell and then see a fish walking on spidery mechanical legs. Soon more creatures follow, and the strange invasion spreads far beyond the beach. It is classic Ito, grotesque, unsettling, and darkly funny, and a strong pick for readers who like their horror weird and memorable.
237: Deep-Sea Aquarium Magmell by Kiyomi Sugishita (Yen Press) is a gentle workplace drama about the wonders of the deep ocean. A young man who has loved deep-sea creatures since childhood takes a job at Magmell, an aquarium built far below the ocean's surface. As he learns the ropes, he discovers how much care these strange animals need. It is calm and curious, a great pick for nature lovers and readers who enjoy quiet, heartfelt stories.
239: Clevatess by Yuji Iwahara (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy about an unlikely family. Clevatess, the fearsome King of Dark Beasts, easily defeats the heroes sent to slay him. Then he takes in a human baby and raises one of the fallen heroes as an undead servant to help care for the child. It blends brutal battles with surprising tenderness, and it will appeal to readers who like monster leads and found-family stories.
243: Playing Death Games to Put Food on the Table by BanzaiKotobukiDaienkai, Yushi Ukai, and Nekometaru (Yen Press) is a psychological thriller with a cool-headed lead. Yuki is a young woman who takes part in deadly games for prize money and treats it like a job. She has a goal most players never reach: surviving ninety-nine games. Each game is a new trap to outthink, and it suits readers who enjoy survival puzzles and tense mind games.
245: Seeds of Anxiety by Masaaki Nakayama (Yen Press) is a collection of short, creepy horror vignettes. Each piece is only a few pages long, capturing a single frightening moment: a face at the window, a shape in the hallway, something wrong in an ordinary room. There is no long plot, just one jolt after another. It is perfect for horror fans who like quick scares and art that lingers in your mind after the lights go out.
265: Yona of the Dawn by Mizuho Kusanagi (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure about a sheltered princess who finds her strength. Princess Yona of the kingdom of Kouka has lived a pampered life, loved by her gentle father and sweet on her cousin Su-won. On her sixteenth birthday, a shocking betrayal forces her to flee the palace with her loyal bodyguard Hak. This 3-in-1 edition is a great way to start a sweeping story full of action, humor, and heart.
269: Buying a Classmate Once a Week by Usa Haneda with illustrations by U35 (Yen Press) is a quiet yuri romance light novel. High schooler Shiori Miyagi has an unusual arrangement with her classmate Hazuki Sendai: once a week, Miyagi pays her five thousand yen, and Sendai does whatever Miyagi asks. At school they barely speak. It is a slow, introspective story about two guarded girls, and it suits readers who like tension and complicated feelings.
276: And Then There Were None by Agatha Christie, adapted by Aya Nikaido (Viz Media), is a manga version of the classic mystery thriller. Ten strangers are invited to a mansion on a remote island, but their host never appears. At dinner, a recorded voice accuses each of them of murder, and then the guests begin to die one by one. It is a faithful, atmospheric take on Christie's famous puzzle for mystery fans old and new.
295: Magical Explorer by Iris (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy about a gamer reborn inside his favorite game. A devoted fan wakes up as Kousuke Takioto, a minor character in the adult fantasy game Magical Explorer, cast as the hero's best friend. Since he knows the game inside and out, he sets out to train hard and become stronger than the story intends. It suits readers who like isekai, game mechanics, and a lead who plays smart.
301: Polly and the Pirates by Ted Naifeh (Oni Press) is a swashbuckling adventure for younger readers. Polly Pringle is a proper young lady at a strict boarding school who dreams of pirate tales but would never break the rules. Then a band of pirates kidnaps her, convinced she is the daughter of their legendary lost captain, the Pirate Queen Meg. It is full of humor, sea battles, and spirit, and it is a fun pick for kids and families.
302: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap by Akira Himekawa (Viz Media) is an all-ages fantasy adventure based on the video game. When the sorcerer Vaati turns Princess Zelda to stone, young Link sets out to save her. Along the way he teams up with Ezlo, a cranky talking cap who can shrink Link down to the size of the tiny Minish people. It is a light, funny quest that suits kids and longtime Zelda fans alike.
304: The Guin Saga by Kaoru Kurimoto (Vertical) is a sweeping heroic fantasy. In a haunted forest at the edge of the kingdoms, a warrior with the head of a leopard wakes with no memory except a single name: Guin. He soon crosses paths with Rinda and Remus, the royal twins of a fallen kingdom, and becomes their fierce protector. It is classic sword-and-sorcery, and a good pick for readers who like mystery, battles, and old-school adventure.
305: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask by Akira Himekawa (Viz Media) is an all-ages fantasy adventure based on the video game. While searching for a lost friend, Link is ambushed by the mischievous Skull Kid, who wears a strange mask. Link follows him into Termina, a land where the moon is set to fall in just three days. It is a slightly darker Zelda tale with plenty of heart, and it suits kids and longtime fans alike.
306: Accel World by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action light novel from the creator of Sword Art Online. Haruyuki Arita is a short, overweight middle schooler who escapes bullies by playing virtual squash alone. One day, Kuroyukihime, the school's beautiful and mysterious student council vice president, offers him a program called Brain Burst, which can speed up his thoughts. It is fast and full of battles, and it suits fans of virtual-world stories.
309: X by CLAMP (Viz Media) is a dark supernatural drama about the end of the world. Kamui Shiro returns to Tokyo after years away, carrying powerful psychic abilities and a destiny he wants nothing to do with. He finds two opposing groups waiting for him, one fighting to protect humanity and one seeking to destroy it, and both believe his choice will decide everything. It is moody, dramatic, and beautifully drawn, a strong pick for CLAMP fans.
310: Sword Art Online by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action light novel about a game no one can log out of. When the virtual reality game Sword Art Online launches, ten thousand players discover they are trapped inside, and dying in the game means dying in real life. The only way out is to clear all one hundred floors of the castle Aincrad. Kirito, a skilled solo player, sets out to survive. It suits fans of gaming adventure.
313: Blade of the Immortal by Hiroaki Samura (Dark Horse) is a gritty samurai action series. Manji is a swordsman cursed with immortality: strange bloodworms in his body heal every wound. To lift the curse, he vows to kill one thousand evil men. Then a young girl named Rin hires him to help avenge her parents' murder. With striking brush-style art and intense sword fights, it is a great choice for fans of dark historical action.
317: Katanagatari by Nisio Isin (Kodansha) is a historical action adventure with sharp, playful dialogue. Shichika Yasuri lives on a remote island practicing a sword style that uses no sword at all. One day the ambitious strategist Togame arrives and recruits him for a mission: to collect the twelve legendary Deviant Blades made by the swordsmith Kiki Shikizaki. It is witty, stylish, and full of duels, a good pick for fans of the anime and of Isin's writing.
318: Dragon Half by Ryusuke Mita (Seven Seas) is a goofy fantasy comedy. Mink is a cheerful girl who is half human and half dragon, born to a dragon mother and a knight father. She is madly in love with Dick Saucer, a famous dragon-slaying knight who also happens to be a pop star. The trouble is, he slays dragons for a living. It is silly, fast-paced, and full of slapstick, a fun read for fans of classic anime-style comedy.
324: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney by Kenji Kuroda (Kodansha) is a courtroom mystery based on the video game series. Phoenix Wright is a determined young defense attorney who takes on cases that look hopeless, defending clients everyone else assumes are guilty. With help from his friends, he digs for clues, catches witnesses in lies, and turns trials around. It is funny, clever, and a great pick for game fans and anyone who loves a good mystery.
325: Mobile Police Patlabor by Masami Yuki (Viz Media) is a sci-fi workplace comedy about giant robots on the police force. In near-future Tokyo, large robots called Labors do construction work, and a special police unit pilots Patlabors to stop Labor-related crime. Noa Izumi, a cheerful young recruit who loves robots, joins the team and names her machine Alphonse. It is lively and down-to-earth, a good pick for mecha fans who like humor and heart.
327: There's No Freaking Way I'll Be Your Lover! Unless... by Teren Mikami with illustrations by Eku Takeshima (Seven Seas) is a yuri romantic comedy light novel. Renako Amaori was a loner in middle school, so she reinvents herself to join the popular crowd in high school. She becomes close friends with Mai Ouzuka, the most glamorous girl in school, until Mai confesses her love. Renako insists she only wants to be friends. It is funny, heartfelt, and full of chaos.
335: I'll Give It My All... Tomorrow by Shunju Aono (Viz Media) is a bittersweet comedy about a midlife do-over. Shizuo Oguro is forty-one when he quits his job, announcing he wants to find himself. He eventually decides to become a manga artist, much to the dismay of his father and teenage daughter, who share a home with him. It is gently funny and honest about failure and hope, a good pick for adults who like slice-of-life stories.
336: Planetes by Makoto Yukimura (Tokyopop) is a thoughtful sci-fi drama about everyday life in space. In the 2070s, Hachimaki works as a debris collector, clearing junk from orbit so ships and stations stay safe. He dreams of owning his own spaceship one day, while working alongside a crew of colorful coworkers. It is grounded, human, and quietly moving, a great pick for readers who like realistic science fiction and stories about chasing dreams.
338: Star Wars Rebels by Akira Aoki (Yen Press) is a sci-fi adventure based on the animated series. On the Empire-controlled planet Lothal, Ezra Bridger is a street-smart teenager surviving on his own. When he crosses paths with the crew of the starship Ghost, a small band of rebels fighting the Empire, he finds himself pulled into their missions. It is fast and fun, a good pick for kids and Star Wars fans of all ages.
339: Usagi Yojimbo by Stan Sakai (Dark Horse) is a samurai adventure set in a version of feudal Japan populated by animals. Miyamoto Usagi is a rabbit ronin, a masterless samurai who wanders the land as a bodyguard for hire. Along the road he meets bandits, ninja, monsters, and old friends, and he always tries to do the right thing. It mixes action, humor, and history, and it is a great read for all ages.
340: Space Dandy by Masafumi Harada (Yen Press) is a sci-fi comedy based on the anime. Dandy is a cool-acting alien hunter who travels the galaxy looking for rare, undiscovered aliens to register for cash. He is joined by Meow, a lazy cat-like alien, and QT, an old cleaning robot, and their adventures rarely go as planned. It is goofy and carefree, a fun pick for fans of the anime and of space comedies.
341: Lunar Legend Tsukihime by Sasaki Shonen (Dr. Master) is a supernatural action story based on the visual novel. After a childhood accident, Shiki Tohno can see lines of death running through people and objects, and cutting them destroys whatever they mark. Wearing special glasses, he lives a fairly normal life, until he meets a mysterious blond woman and things take a terrible turn. It is dark and stylish, a good pick for fans of vampire stories and Type-Moon.
342: Gente by Natsume Ono (Viz Media) is a gentle slice-of-life follow-up to Ristorante Paradiso. At Casetta dell'Orso, a small restaurant in Rome, the waiters are all distinguished older men in glasses, and the customers come back as much for them as for the food. Each chapter looks closer at the staff and the people around them. It is warm, quiet, and grown-up, perfect for readers who like character studies and cozy settings.
350: Itaewon Class by Gwang Jin (Ize Press) is a revenge drama about a young man who refuses to back down. Park Sae-ro-yi is expelled from high school after standing up to a bully, the son of a powerful restaurant company chairman. When his life falls apart, he vows to take that company down and starts by opening a small bar in Seoul's Itaewon district. It is about grit and found family, and fans of the K-drama will enjoy it.
352: Orochi by Kazuo Umezz (Viz Media) is a classic horror anthology. Orochi is a mysterious, ageless girl with strange powers who drifts from place to place, quietly watching ordinary families. In each story she takes on a new identity and witnesses the jealousy, fear, and cruelty that can hide behind closed doors. It is unsettling and often heartbreaking, a great pick for horror fans who want to see where a lot of modern manga horror began.
353: Nightschool: The Weirn Books by Svetlana Chmakova (Yen Press) is a supernatural mystery. Alex is a young weirn, a kind of witch, who has been homeschooled, but her older sister Sarah works as a keeper at the Nightschool, a school for supernatural students that opens after dark. When Sarah suddenly vanishes and no one seems to remember her, Alex sets out to find out what happened. It blends magic, friendship, and mystery for teen readers.
354: The Saga of Tanya the Evil by Carlo Zen (Yen Press) is a military fantasy light novel with a dark sense of humor. A ruthless salaryman is killed and, after defying a being who claims to be God, is reborn as a little girl named Tanya in a world at war. Gifted with magic, she joins the army, planning a safe career behind the lines. It is sharp and strategic, a great pick for fans of war stories and antiheroes.
355: Do You Love Your Mom and Her Two-Hit Multi-Target Attacks? by Dachima Inaka (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy about a very awkward adventure. High schooler Masato Oosuki is thrilled to be pulled into a fantasy game world, until he learns his doting mom Mamako is coming along. Worse, she turns out to be far stronger than he is. It is silly and good-natured, a fun pick for readers who enjoy isekai comedy and family humor.
357: Hazure Skill: The Guild Member with a Worthless Skill Is Actually a Legendary Assassin by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a fantasy action light novel. Roland was once the most feared assassin around, but he has retired to a quiet job as a clerk at the adventurers guild. He wants a peaceful life, yet his skills keep drawing him into trouble. It is light and fast, a good pick for readers who like overpowered heroes trying to stay low-key.
377: My Instant Death Ability Is So Overpowered by Tsuyoshi Fujitaka is a dark fantasy comedy about an unbeatable hero. Yogiri Takatou sleeps through the moment his class is summoned to another world, so he wakes up with no special skills and is left behind as useless. What no one realizes is that Yogiri can kill anything just by wishing it dead. It is darkly funny and fast, a good pick for readers who like overpowered leads.
381: Queen Emeraldas by Leiji Matsumoto (Kodansha) is a space opera from the creator of Captain Harlock. Hiroshi Umino is a young man determined to build his own spaceship and fly free among the stars, even if it means struggling alone. Along the way he crosses paths with Emeraldas, a scarred, legendary space pirate who sails the galaxy aboard her ship, the Queen Emeraldas. It is moody and romantic, a great pick for fans of classic sci-fi.
387: Magia Record: Puella Magi Madoka Magica Side Story by Magica Quartet (Yen Press) is a magical girl fantasy set in the Madoka Magica universe. Iroha Tamaki is a magical girl haunted by the feeling that she has forgotten something important, and she soon realizes it is her little sister, Ui. Following rumors, she travels to Kamihama City, where magical girls are said to find salvation. It suits fans of the franchise and readers who like dark magical girl stories.
392: Black Jack by Osamu Tezuka (Vertical) is a medical drama from the godfather of manga. Black Jack is a brilliant surgeon with no medical license and a scarred face who charges outrageous fees for impossible operations. Each chapter brings a new patient, from the rich and powerful to the desperate, along with his loyal young assistant Pinoko. It is gripping, thoughtful, and surprisingly moving, and this deluxe edition is a great way to read a true classic.
